feedback: Approved for the race. This candidate changes one variable from the best raced design: kp 3.8 to 4.0, with kd 0.8, base_speed 1.3, ki 0, line_loss 'last_direction' and geometry unchanged. Iteration 3 showed that raising kp from 3.5 to 3.8 (with kd 0.6 to 0.7) lifted the score from 556.7 to 634.7 and slalom progress from 0.30 to 0.49. Iteration 4 (kp 3.8, kd 0.8, score 653.0, the best so far) kept the oval at 20/20 with max_error 0.011 and reduced s-bend steering_oscillation to 0.33. Iteration 2 showed that base_speed 1.2 cost more on the oval and s-bend (score 521.7) than it gained on the slalom, so speed stays at 1.3. The step is small and well isolated, so it is a cheap test of whether steering authority still limits the slalom. Its main risk is that kp 4.0 pushes s-bend steering_oscillation back above the 0.33 to 0.37 range, or starts oval exits. The slalom still ends off track in every run, so the telemetry is needed before further change. Read per-track finish counts, max_error, steering_oscillation and slalom progress against iteration 4. Note that kd 0.7 to 0.8 lowered slalom progress (0.49 to 0.46) while it helped the s-bend, so do not treat kd as a slalom lever.
requested_changes: After the race: if the oval holds at 19/20 or better, s-bend steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.35, and slalom progress rises above 0.49, keep kp 4.0 with kd 0.8 and try kp 4.2 to see whether steering authority is still the limit.

After the race: if the oval drops to 18/20 or below, or s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.37, return to the best raced design (kp 3.8, kd 0.8, score 653.0) rather than adjusting kd, since kd 0.8 gave the best s-bend result so far.

After the race: if slalom max_error stays above 0.06 with line_loss_events near 1.0 while the oval still finishes, test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' only if the last valid signal shows a consistent one-sided exit; keep ki at 0 and base_speed at 1.3.
